the תנו רבנן of 65a.9, named תנא דבי רב by the stam at 66a.1
פריך רב אחאי (65b.8); אלא אמר רב אחאי (65b.10)

props.gloss_en: one that does not have [them] now and will grow [them] after a time, such as the zachal -- is permitted
R' Elazar b'R' Yosei: 'which have [lo] kera'ayim' -- even though it does not have [them] now and will grow [them] after a time
what is the zachal? Abaye: askara
arbeh -- this is the govai (both schools: 65a.9, 65a.10)
salam -- this is the rashon
chargol -- this is the nippul
chagav -- this is the nadyan
[lemino] comes to include the tziporet keramim (both schools: 65a.9 among the four; 65a.10-65b.1 from 'arbeh ... lemino')
and the yochana yerushalmit
and the artzuvya
and the razbanit -- the four inclusions of the four 'leminehu'
these are generalizations of generalizations, and these are details of details
one that comes and has a gabachat -- from where? the verse says 'salam' -- this is the nippul
'leminehu' [after salam] -- to include the ushkaf
one that comes and has a tail -- from where? the verse says 'chargol' -- this is the rashon
'leminehu' [after chargol] -- to include the karsefet
and the shachalanit
one that comes and its head is long is [kosher]: so too any that has four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and whose wings cover most of it
but the tzartzur has four legs, four wings, jumping legs and wings covering most of it -- might it be permitted? the verse says 'chagav': its name must be chagav
if its name is chagav, might it be [kosher] without all these signs? the verse says 'leminehu': not until it has all these signs
Rav Achai: salam is superfluous -- let the Merciful One not write 'salam', and let it be derived from arbeh and chargol
why do I need the salam the Merciful One wrote? if it is not needed for its own matter, apply it to the matter of [a grasshopper] whose head is long
over what do the tanna of the school of Rav and the tanna of the school of R' Yishmael disagree? they disagree over one whose head is long
a [grasshopper] whose head is long is not permitted -- the school of Rav's side of the dispute the stam names at 66a.1 (its baraita at 65a.9 does not say so)

the school of Rav holds: 'which have kera'ayim' is a klal; arbeh, salam, chargol, chagav, leminehu are the prat; klal and prat -- the klal holds only what is in the prat: of its kind, yes; not of its kind, no
and [leminehu] includes what resembles it on two sides
the school of R' Yishmael holds: 'which have kera'ayim' is a klal, arbeh-salam-chargol-chagav the prat, 'leminehu' a klal again; klal, prat and klal -- you derive only what is like the prat
and [leminehu] includes whatever resembles it on one side
the tanna of the school of R' Yishmael does expound klalim and pratim of this kind [though the two klalim are unlike]
and what we also say elsewhere -- that the tanna of the school of R' Yishmael expounds klalim and pratim of this kind -- is from here
